title: Mini-bundle PRD: Unified inference surface for chat, completion, embeddings, and rerank with launch surge plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: High-level PRD to deliver a compact, production-ready 'mini-bundle' that exposes a consistent API surface for chat, completion, embeddings, and rerank use cases. The intent is to offer a single onboarding flow, one billing SKU with per-route knobs, and an operational surge/rollback plan for launch day. This ticket scopes the product requirements, acceptance criteria, risks, and a tactical launch checklist for a targeted GA to early enterprise customers.
background: We have multiple Large PRDs covering the full hosted API family. This effort is a deliberately constrained bundle (MVP) to speed time-to-value for teams that need a single integration covering the most common patterns: single-turn generation, chat turn sequences, vector embedding generation, and rerank scoring pipelines. Key differences from larger PRDs: tighter acceptance gates, explicit surge controls, and a built-in sampling quality monitor tied to rollout gates.
goals: Deliver a single, documented API path that supports chat, completion, embeddings, and rerank with consistent authentication and billing
Provide per-route configuration: max_tokens, temperature, top_p, embedding_model, rerank_model and deterministic fallback mapping
Define launch operational plan that prevents capacity overload via adaptive throttles and a tiered fallback to smaller models/regions
Ship a monitoring plan that samples 0.5% of responses for quality evaluation and flags regression against a baseline prompt set
non_goals: Full multi-modal support (images/audio) in this mini-bundle
Advanced model orchestration policies (A/B weighted routing across unlimited variants) beyond simple canary and fallback
Enterprise-only Dedicated capacity contracts — this targets hosted tier first
requirements: API: Single endpoint group /v1/inference with mode param: {mode: "chat|completion|embedding|rerank"}
SDKs: Expose identical surface in SDKs (python/js) with clear defaults and per-route overrides
Billing: One SKU 'mini_bundle' with per-token generation and per-embedding unit rates; explicit metering for rerank scoring calls
Routing: Support region preference and a fallback route list; fallback must preserve response semantics within 95% of acceptance tests
Rate limits & quotas: Configurable per-tenant soft-limit + hard-limit; a surge policy that reduces batch size and routes to fallback models under sustained queue growth
Observability: Token-level cost, per-request latency, sample payloads (0.5%), and a regression alert if sampled quality score drops by >= 6% vs baseline
Security/compliance: All requests logged with request_id and redaction rules; ensure KMS integration for customer-managed keys is documented for Private later
acceptance_criteria: API contract: OpenAPI entry and SDK surfaces pass contract linting and automated smoke tests
Functional tests: Chat single-turn and multi-turn (3 turns) acceptance suite passes with stability >= 99% over 24h soak
Embedding parity: Embedding model produces vectors within 2% cosine similarity of reference embedding for canonical dataset
Rerank correctness: Top-1 rerank precision on benchmark set >= 88% and latency P95 <= 220ms in hosted region
Billing validation: Billing meter events emitted for every request type and aggregated values match simulated invoice within 0.5%
Safety & redaction: Automated PII redaction hooks exercised and verified in 1000 sample requests

Surge behavior: Under load test (2x expected QPS sustained for 30m) the system enforces surge throttle and fallback route within 60s, with successful degradation behavior (no unhandled 5xx spikes >0.5%)
Canary and rollback: Canary cohort (5% traffic) does not regress metrics for 4 consecutive hours, otherwise automatic rollback to previous model happens
Docs & quickstart: Console quickstart, API docs, and example notebooks present and validated by Solutions Engineering
out_of_scope: Dedicated capacity provisioning flows for this mini-bundle (handled by Dedicated roadmap)
Customer-managed on-prem installation in GA (Private flagged for later cycle)
Complex retraining/inference pipelines or multi-stage retrieval chains — only single call rerank is supported
dependencies: ENG-22111 (runtime: per-request sampling and trace IDs)
risks: Surge underestimation: underestimated launch demand could exhaust GPU pools; mitigated by conservative initial quota and manual surge escalation playbook
Quality regressions due to fallback: cheaper fallback models may produce unacceptable outputs — sampled quality monitor and rollback gates required
Billing mismatch: complexity in metering different call types could produce unexpected invoices for customers; bill validation harness required
Docs/UX confusion: single endpoint with mode param may be confusing; provide strong examples and per-mode templates in SDKs
metrics: Adoption: number of unique tenants calling mini_bundle endpoint in first 30 days
Latency: P95 latency for each mode (chat/completion/embedding/rerank)
Quality: sampled quality score delta vs baseline prompt set (daily)
Cost: average cost-per-1k-token and per-embedding unit by workload
Reliability: % requests successful (2xx) and 5xx rate under load
Billing accuracy: variance between simulated invoice and production invoices
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): SDK + API + docs internal preview with Redwood teams only
Phase 1 (alpha): Invite 5 strategic customers, conservative quotas, 1-week canary; active SRE monitoring and daily review
Phase 2 (beta): Open to self-serve signups with default quotas lowered and surge protections enabled; monitor for two weeks
Phase 3 (GA): Full listing in Console, marketing announcement, quotas increased per usage tiers with sustained SLOs
launch_checklist: Create OpenAPI spec and publish to docs site
SDK releases (python/js) with example notebooks and unit tests
Billing hooks validated end-to-end with sandbox tenants
SRE runbook: surge playbook, escalation matrix, rollback steps
Monitoring dashboards: latency/cost/quality panels configured and alerted
Canary configuration: 5% routing rule and automated rollback triggers
Legal/safety signoff: PII redaction validated and incident response contact added
Support training: playbook and FAQ created for Support and Solutions Engineering
Runload tests: 2x expected QPS sustained 30m without >0.5% 5xx spikes
Smoke tests: end-to-end quickstart validated by two different engineers
engineering_notes: Runtime changes required: per-request sampling hook, fallback routing semantics, and surge throttle metrics. Engineering should run an extended 24h soak test on staging with realistic prompt distributions supplied by Solutions Engineering. Coordinate with billing team to ensure meter event shapes are stable before SDK GA.
qa_plan: Automated acceptance suites for each mode, plus 24h soak and the surge scenario test. QA to validate sampled quality pipeline and alerting. Manual regression checklist for SDK examples and docs. Use a reserved test tenant for billing validation.
